title: Bond energies

draft.title: Bond energies
card: Breaking a bond takes in energy. Making a bond releases energy. The bond energy is the energy needed to break one mole of a particular bond, in kJ/mol.
In a reaction, bonds in the reactants break and new bonds form in the products. ΔH ≈ energy to break bonds - energy released making bonds.
If more energy is released making bonds than is taken in breaking bonds, ΔH is negative. If less is released, ΔH is positive.
Bond energies are averages over many molecules, so ΔH found this way is only an estimate. Each bond is counted once for every mole of it in the equation.
draft.remember: ΔH is roughly energy in to break bonds minus energy out from making bonds.

a.q: In a reaction, the bonds formed in the products release more energy than the bonds broken in the reactants take in. What is true of ΔH?
a.why: ΔH is energy to break bonds minus energy released making bonds. Releasing more than is taken in gives a negative value. A positive ΔH would need the energy taken in to break bonds to be the larger amount.
a.clue: Subtract the energy released from the energy taken in.

b.q: For H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl, breaking 1 mol of H-H (436 kJ/mol) and 1 mol of Cl-Cl (243 kJ/mol) takes in energy. Making 2 mol of H-Cl (432 kJ/mol) releases energy. What is the estimated ΔH?
b.why: Energy taken in is 436 + 243 = 679 kJ. Energy released is 2 × 432 = 864 kJ. ΔH = 679 - 864 = -185 kJ, so the reaction is exothermic. The value +185 comes from subtracting the wrong way round.
b.clue: Count two moles of H-Cl bonds formed, then take released from taken in.

check.summary: No problems found. The bond energy values are standard, and the working (679 − 864 = −185 kJ/mol) is correct.
